A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChaosNexus and retain identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, and appendices. The complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial rewriting and expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-system and WEATHER-5K forecasting results, component ablations, scaling experiments, and attention and expert-activation analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments and analyses, including revised synthetic results, PDE forecasting, controlled Lorenz96 experiments, expert pruning, and weather results stratified by latitude.

M1.justification: The core ScaleFormer architecture, MoE routing, wavelet fingerprint, and composite loss remain unchanged. v2 Appendix B.6 adds a limited inference adaptation for PDE fields: project vorticity into 16 PCA components, forecast those components, and inverse-transform predictions for field-space evaluation.

E1.justification: The synthetic ODE corpus and WEATHER-5K coverage are retained. v2 adds forecasting of a Navier–Stokes Von Kármán vortex street, substantially extending evaluation into PDE dynamics. Electricity, ETT, Exchange Rate, and Traffic data are additionally used for spectral comparisons, rather than forecasting benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 adds DynaMix, Parrot, and additional fine-tuned Chronos variants to the synthetic comparison. Weather comparisons expand beyond the previous system-specific models to include Panda and other foundation models. iTransformer already appeared in v1's weather figures; its expanded description is not a newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds Lyapunov-exponent and spectral-energy error metrics, controlled Lorenz96 forcing experiments, and PDE protocols involving PCA and field-space evaluation. It also revises stated settings: Chronos fine-tuning uses batch size 128 in v1 versus 512 per device in v2, and the founding population changes from 135 to 129. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained component removals, scaling, and attention analyses, v2 adds expert clustering, gating entropy and targeted pruning; alternative fingerprints; MMD weight and kernel sensitivity; controlled spectral-complexity tests; latitude-specific weather analysis; and structural comparisons of training and held-out equations. These test substantially more questions about mechanisms, robustness, and generalization.

E5.justification: v1 already reports 95% confidence intervals in figures. v2 explicitly labels the main numerical and ablation tables as mean ± 95% CI, adds Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing in Figure 3, and reports inference-time means and standard deviations over 1,000 runs. It does not establish increased forecasting training repetitions.

E6.justification: Synthetic scores are substantially revised: ChaosNexus sMAPE@128 changes from 34.401 to 68.901 and Dstsp from 1.409 to 1.206 between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. Ablation values also change, and many new results are added. Parrot now has lower Dfrac and MELRw than ChaosNexus. The unchanged stated sMAPE formula leaves the large score revisions unexplained.

T1.justification: v2 introduces mathematical definitions for the added Lyapunov and spectral-energy errors and states a fingerprint Lipschitz bound in Appendix I, Equation 29. Existing wavelet and MMD mathematics is retained. Much of Appendix I provides conceptual operator and dynamical-system interpretations; it does not supply new proofs establishing its generalization claims.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds a new universal foundation-model paradigm and diversity-driven scaling. v2 acknowledges existing ODE foundation models and centers its contribution on hierarchical temporal and spectral modeling. The title explicitly narrows the framing to ODE-based systems, and the abstract describes point-wise accuracy as competitive. The scaling finding remains in Appendix B.3.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations: patch merging is interpreted as spectral filtering, routing similarities as transfer of physical priors, and expert representations through vector-field and Koopman analogies. It also interprets the new pruning, fingerprint, and MMD experiments and discusses inference-cost tradeoffs and PDE transfer through PCA. Several explanations are stronger than the accompanying demonstrations establish.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents three-channel training and full-variable inference, the default Base variant, AdamW settings, learning-rate scheduling, warmup, clipping, hardware, BF16, and training time. It also supplies simulation and preprocessing details for new experiments. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility documentation; the ChaosNexus code address was already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning relative to Panda and newly discussed DynaMix, locating novelty in architectural treatment of spectral heterogeneity rather than introducing the foundation-model paradigm itself. It adds Parrot and other relevant references and explicitly acknowledges Panda's earlier system-diversity scaling result in Appendix B.3.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, conclusion, and architecture exposition undergo substantial rewriting. The experimental narrative is reorganized, scaling moves from the main text to Appendix B.3, and the appendices are extensively restructured. These changes exceed routine wording edits or additions of scientific content alone.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from one-column to two-column layout, expands benchmark tables, reorganizes weather plots, and adds numerous spectral, PDE, routing, pruning, and dataset-analysis displays. Existing scaling and diagnostic figures are relocated, while the architecture diagram and several forecasting showcases remain identifiable.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides stronger comparators, more targeted tests of architectural choices, clearer prior-work attribution, and substantially better training documentation. These improve scrutiny and reproducibility. However, substantial score revisions remain unexplained, Appendix B.2 retains ablation percentages inconsistent with Table 2, and Tables 1 and 2 give different uncertainty values for the same full-model MELRw result. These reporting problems limit confidence in the expanded evidence and the overall quality gain.
